agent.name: Emerging Technology Landscape Agent
agent.specialty: Dated technology landscape, alternatives, ecosystems, and decision-relevant monitoring

analytical_question: As of 17 November 2026, which alternatives and observable signals should the owner of a hypothetical small U.S. homeware retailer consider during the six-week review from 13 November to 25 December 2026 before deciding whether to authorize a bounded comparison for internal campaign concepts? This assessment used read-only public-source research. No retailer systems, catalog assets, or image-generation tools were accessed. The owner is the proposed decision authority, and trial authority and tool permissions remain unconfirmed.
general_et_finding: Latent diffusion is a documented historical architecture for text-conditioned synthesis. A current supplier also documents image generation and reference-based editing interfaces. Reference-based editing describes a workflow and does not identify the underlying model architecture. The evidence establishes historical research demonstrations and documented commercial tool access. Independent, reproducible evidence of sustained production performance at the intended scope is missing, including fidelity, repeatability, tail failures, and recovery by model version and workload. Ecosystem diligence remains open on hosting, retention, portability, version stability, support, and exit. Comparable investment, industry adoption, performance, and lifecycle-cost trends are unverified.
application_finding: Qualitative comparison at equivalent scope: disposable internal homeware concept boards. Each option is assessed in the order of capability fit, autonomy and permissions, evidence strength, accountability and recourse, integration and complements, vendor dependence and portability, and full lifecycle cost. Manual or freelance boards: direct control of composition and catalog references, human execution and established access, incumbent use per intake with no measured baseline, identifiable designer and revision path with freelance terms to verify, existing catalog and editing tools, portability subject to source-file handoff and licenses, and unknown labor, fees, review and rework costs. Text-to-image generation: plausible for broad visual exploration with uncertain SKU fidelity, marketer-initiated prompts with tool access and no publishing permission, capability evidence with no matched retailer outcomes, designated human review and rejection, a private concept workspace and catalog-based checks, dependence on supplier terms and versions or on local maintenance with export unverified, and unknown setup, inference, retries, review, remediation and exit costs. Reference-based generation or editing: plausible for composition around approved references with fidelity unverified, marketer-initiated edits requiring input-specific permission, supplier feature evidence with no matched fidelity results, named reviewer and discard or manual correction path, approved assets and catalog-side checks, dependence on upload terms, version and export with portability unverified, and unknown subscription or compute, asset preparation, retries, review, rework and exit costs. These are design judgments. For downstream U.S. advertising, the FTC's guidance explains the statutory prohibition on deceptive advertising under FTC Act Section 5. The Copyright Office's Part 2 report provides federal agency analysis of output copyrightability. Account-specific terms and input permissions require separate review.
organization_specific_finding: The hypothetical retailer has two marketers, existing owner review, a photo catalog, and manual editing competence. The intake confirms no AI-specific sponsor, coordinator, reviewer, protected hours, or approved upload route. Manual or freelance boards are the strongest provisional comparator because the workflow is already in use and can draw on the catalog directly. Focus the review on three signals: viable account terms and export, named ownership and protected capacity, and matched evidence on reference fidelity and all-in effort. The low consequence of discarding private boards supports preparing a reversible comparison. It leaves staffing, permission, and downstream release risks to be resolved.

evidence.claim: The scenario specifies internal concept work, two marketers, an existing manual workflow, independently checked final product photos, and no authorized or executed trial.
evidence.source_or_reference: Attached L9-Y-P prompt packet, CASE CONTEXT and additional_context.
evidence.date_or_recency: Review begins 13 November 2026. Intake read 17 November 2026.
evidence.notes: Applies to one fictional retailer. The referenced source ledger was unavailable in the workspace. Its reported preparer check date provides no independently inspected evidence in this run.

evidence.claim: The authors demonstrate text conditioning for diffusion in a learned latent space and report image synthesis and related editing experiments.
evidence.source_or_reference: Rombach et al., High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models, arXiv abstract, https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.10752.
evidence.evidence_type: Original academic research by the architecture's authors.
evidence.notes: Historical research tasks and benchmarks. The source establishes an architecture and demonstrations. It supplies no independent replication, current retailer operating period, or matched lifecycle-cost comparison.

evidence.claim: OpenAI documents image generation and an edits endpoint that accepts reference images and masks.
evidence.source_or_reference: OpenAI API, Image generation, Edit Images, https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation.
evidence.date_or_recency: Living documentation with no fixed publication date established. Accessed 17 November 2026.
evidence.notes: Describes API operations. Provides no independently verified outcomes, retailer adoption denominator, SKU-fidelity rate, account-specific contractual permission, or basis for classifying the underlying architecture as latent diffusion.

evidence.claim: FTC guidance describes the U.S. truth-in-advertising requirements for businesses.
evidence.source_or_reference: Federal Trade Commission, Advertising FAQs: A Guide for Small Business, https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/advertising-faqs-guide-small-business.
evidence.date_or_recency: FTC guidance retrieved 17 November 2026. Exact publication and provision-specific effective dates were not verified in this review.
evidence.evidence_type: Federal enforcement agency guidance explaining binding U.S. law under FTC Act Section 5.
evidence.notes: Relevant to the retailer in its role as advertiser if an image conveys a product claim to consumers. The intake limits the proposed application to private concepts. This review makes no compliance determination.

evidence.claim: The U.S. Copyright Office published Part 2 of its AI report on copyrightability of generative AI outputs.
evidence.source_or_reference: U.S. Copyright Office, Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Report on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, https://www.copyright.gov/ai/.
evidence.evidence_type: Original federal agency report index and publication record. The report is agency analysis.
evidence.notes: Relevant to a U.S. creator or claimant considering output protection. The report has no provision-specific effective date as legislation. Asset-level rights and supplier terms remain unresolved.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Reference inputs may improve creative control, but documented input support provides no measured assurance that the tool preserves SKU geometry, colors, finishes, or proportions.
Faster initial output could be offset by prompting, reruns, drift checks, owner review, and selective manual reconstruction. Existing boards could retain a lower all-in cost.

Research demonstrations and supplier documentation answer different questions. No independent scope-matched production comparison or verified data on industry adoption, funding, or normalized cost trends was available.

The packet's unverified claim that Agentic AI is production-ready and cheaper than human-supported banking service concerns a different technology, task, and consequence environment. It lacks scope-matched production and lifecycle-cost evidence and provides no support for this decision.
confidence_and_uncertainty: General level: high confidence in the historical architecture and documented API operations, low confidence in comparative current maturity and cost trends. Application level: moderate confidence in the comparison design, low confidence in any claim of fidelity, throughput, or savings. Organization level: moderate confidence that PREPARATION_ONLY fits the stated assumptions, low confidence in future trial feasibility until rights, roles, time, and the manual baseline are verified.
value_opportunity_implication: Generation could expand the range of concepts the owner can review, while approved reference-based editing could help marketers explore scenes around a known product. Either option has a provisional value case only if it delivers reviewable variety at acceptable fidelity and all-in effort against the incumbent on the same briefs.
risk_governance_implication: For any separately authorized evaluation, use only approved input assets and a restricted internal workspace. Log model versions, source assets, reviewer decisions, rework, and disposal. Route rejected concepts out of the workflow and retain independently checked final product photography and the existing release review. Assign an accountable reviewer and a path to withdraw a concept that escapes into downstream use. Verify rights and privacy obligations with a qualified reviewer. Applicable voluntary standards and pending proposals were not established in this run.
recommendation_management_implication: Retain PREPARATION_ONLY. Prepare a matched comparison of manual or freelance boards, text-only generation, and approved reference-based editing using equivalent briefs and a common review rubric. Ask the owner to consider separate trial authorization once terms, staffing, and acceptable thresholds are documented. After authorization, a candidate could displace the incumbent for internal concepts only if matched results meet the owner's fidelity and usability floor, avoid disqualifying failures, and show sufficient all-in improvement including rework and review. Adoption and readiness should validate capacity and workflow fit, governance should verify assets and supplier terms, and the owner should decide whether to authorize or pause.
change_monitoring_triggers: Supplier terms and portability: check official business-account terms, data handling documentation, model lifecycle notices, and export documentation when screening candidates and immediately before any authorization. Recheck upon material provider changes. Proposed owner: designated governance reviewer. Threshold: permitted asset uploads, acceptable retention and reuse terms, and required export capability are documented. If any element is missing or withdrawn, recommend holding or pausing that candidate for owner review.

Readiness: at the first management checkpoint on 20 November 2026 and weekly through the six-week review, check the written owner decision, named coordinator and reviewer, and scheduled protected hours. Proposed owner: retailer owner. Threshold: all roles are accepted and sufficient time is reserved for setup, review, and remediation. Absent coverage keeps the proposal at PREPARATION_ONLY. Documented coverage and a cleared supplier route allow an authorization decision.

Matched fidelity and effort: during a separately authorized evaluation, check the first matched batch and each subsequent batch against identical manual or freelance briefs, a catalog fidelity rubric, and time and cost logs. Proposed owner: designated marketer with owner sign-off. Require acceptable concept quality and fidelity and a meaningful all-in effort or cost improvement. Values are pending retailer agreement and owner approval before launch. A verified unauthorized upload or public release triggers immediate escalation and a proposed pause. A missed target retains the incumbent. Meeting the agreed thresholds supports owner review of the next scope.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: The research owner needs the referenced source ledger or its original URLs to reconcile the evidence reportedly checked on 13 November 2026. Current market rankings, investment and adoption trends remain unsupported.

The governance reviewer needs the exact supplier plan, contract terms, data handling and export provisions, plus catalog and freelancer asset permissions. These gaps block an upload or tool approval decision.

The owner and marketers need a measured incumbent baseline, named trial roles, protected hours, an approved rubric, and versioned matched results. Savings, acceptance rates, sustained reliability, and replacement suitability remain undetermined. No trial was run.
A qualified U.S. reviewer needs the actual input rights, intended output use, and consumer-facing release process before offering an applicability or compliance conclusion.
